summary: HTTP transport foundation: HttpRequestEngine wraps an httpx.Client and applies a RequestPolicy (retry with exponential backoff and jitter, per-phase timeouts, request-local redirect limits, one auth refresh on 401) to buffered and streaming requests. It maps httpx exceptions and non-2xx statuses to a typed HttpTransportError hierarchy that is independent of StorageError, and redacts URL userinfo from error messages, response URLs and displayed exception chains. Policies, responses and errors are stdlib-only; only the engine needs httpx and is resolved lazily behind the [http] extra.
key_classes: HttpRequestEngine — executes requests over an injected httpx.Client with retry, 401 auth refresh, Retry-After handling, redirect limits, location checks and error mapping
RequestPolicy — frozen composite of retry/timeout/redirect policies plus auth_refresh_on_401; with_timeout/with_retry/with_redirect derive copies
RetryPolicy — frozen retry settings (max_attempts=3, backoff, retry_on_status=(429,500,502,503,504), retry_unsafe_methods=False, max_retry_after=120s)
RedirectPolicy — frozen follow_redirects/max_redirects (default 10), enforced per call
HttpResponse — frozen fully-buffered response with .text and .json() (raises HttpDecodeError)
HttpStreamResponse — wrapper over a streaming httpx.Response exposing iter_bytes/iter_text/read/close and a redacted url
HttpTransportError — base of the HTTP error tree; string args are userinfo-redacted
HttpResponseError — status-bearing error with status_code, headers, body_preview, url, method; HttpRateLimitError adds retry_after
AuthStrategy / RefreshableAuthStrategy — runtime-checkable protocols (auth_protocol.py) for credential injection and refresh consumed by the engine
key_functions: HttpRequestEngine.request(method, url, *, headers=None, content=None, stream=None, params=None, policy=None) -> HttpResponse — buffered request with retries and error mapping

HttpRequestEngine.stream(method, url, *, headers=None, content=None, params=None, policy=None) -> ContextManager[HttpStreamResponse] — retries/refreshes only before yielding; no replay once body consumption starts
map_status_to_error(status_code) -> type[HttpResponseError] — most specific error class for a 4xx/5xx code; ValueError otherwise
redact_userinfo(text) -> str — replace scheme://userinfo@ with scheme://***@ (redact.py, not exported)
extension_points: Implement RefreshableAuthStrategy (apply/refresh/get_headers) to supply live-refreshing auth headers; connections.auth_strategy.OAuth2RefreshableAuthStrategy is the in-tree implementation
Pass location_check=callable(url) to HttpRequestEngine to veto any outgoing request, including redirects and auth-flow follow-ups
Override behaviour per call via policy=RequestPolicy(...) or derive with RequestPolicy.with_* helpers
Inject a pre-built httpx.Client (custom transport, e.g. httpx.MockTransport, proxies, TLS) — the engine never constructs its own client
lifecycle_notes: The engine borrows the httpx.Client; it never closes it. Client lifetime belongs to HTTPConnection or the caller.
HttpRequestEngine is resolved by module __getattr__; importing it without httpx raises MissingExtraError naming [http]. Policies, responses and errors import on a base install.
stream() closes the httpx response when the context exits; errors raised during body consumption are mapped but never retried.
Client-level auth (client.auth) drives the auth flow; individual sends use a no-op auth so httpx-stripped Authorization headers on cross-origin redirects are not reapplied.

Retries on 429 ignore method safety; other retryable statuses and transport errors require an idempotent method (or retry_unsafe_methods) and a replayable body. A 401 refresh retry does not count against max_attempts.
documentation_hooks: HTTP engine guide: retry, timeout and redirect policies with defaults table
HTTP error hierarchy reference and status-code mapping table
Security note: URL userinfo redaction scope and limits (display only, not secret erasure)
LocationPolicy enforcement on every HTTP send including redirects
examples: examples/http_engine/example.py — retry on a transient 503 and typed HttpNotFoundError without retry, via httpx.MockTransport
examples/http_engine/README.md — recipe narrative and expected output
risks: HttpTransportError does not subclass StorageError (errors.py docstring); callers using the engine directly must catch the HTTP hierarchy, while facade users see StorageError translations — two error vocabularies for HTTP.

request(stream=...) reads a stream body into bytes up front but still gates retries on stream.seekable(), so a non-seekable stream body is never retried even though the bytes are already buffered (engine.py _is_body_replayable/_resolve_body).
stream() accepts only content=bytes, not a stream body, and sets body_preview=None on error responses, unlike request().
Userinfo redaction is display-only: hidden __context__, request objects and traceback locals can still hold credentials; query-string tokens are not redacted (README 'Storage errors').
map_status_to_error raises ValueError for non-4xx/5xx codes; a 1xx final status reaching _raise_for_status would surface as ValueError rather than an HTTP error.
Backoff uses time.sleep in the calling thread; large backoff_max/max_retry_after values block callers.
open_questions: Should map_status_to_error (in module __all__) be exported from the package root or treated as internal?
Should request() treat a fully-read stream body as replayable for retries?

_send_with_redirects enforces per-call max_redirects and location_check on every request; request()/stream() retry logic
